standard.title: Experiment, document and reflect on visual arts practice
standard.description: experiment with, document and reflect on ways to use a range of visual conventions, visual arts processes, and materials
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can experiment with a range of materials and processes, document discoveries through annotation, and use visual arts language to reflect (AC9AVA4D01). They have begun investigating composition. They have not yet produced systematic logbook-style documentation, experimented with Augmented Reality or cross-arts visual mapping, or applied observational drawing across multiple representational modes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students experiment with, document and reflect on ways to use a range of visual conventions, visual arts processes and materials, using their documentation as a source for informed making choices.

nodes.label: Systematic documentation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can document experiments systematically — recording what was tried, what resulted, and what it means for future making.
nodes.minimum_width: Document at least one experiment in a logbook or visual diary — record what was tried, what the result was, and one implication for future making.
nodes.typical_width: Maintain a developing documentation record across multiple experiments; use Viewpoints questions to annotate processes; connect discoveries to informed future choices; build a body of documented practice.
wider: Create a systematic comparison of analog and digital simulations of the same material — record findings in a logbook and draw conclusions about when each is preferable
Document the steps of a printmaking process — record variations (colour changes, progressive texture additions) and reflect on what each variation produces
nodes.hinge_reason: Systematic documentation is the key new demand at Y5-6 — students who do not maintain records of experiments cannot make informed choices in subsequent making. The documentation is what converts experiments into a knowledge base.

response_modes.reason: Documentation habits require consistent expectation across multiple sessions to become genuinely systematic. Students who document only when required develop superficial records — the habit needs consolidation through repeated practice.

success_criteria: Produces at least one documented experiment that records what was tried and what resulted
Draws at least one implication for future making from the documentation

nodes.label: Multiple approaches to representation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use multiple approaches to represent the same subject — observational drawing, gestural drawing, photographic overlay, abstract — and reflect on what each approach can and cannot communicate.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two different approaches to represent the same subject; describe what each approach communicates differently.
nodes.typical_width: Explore and reflect on observational and gestural drawing as different ways to describe an object; combine imaginative drawing over realistic photographs; investigate printmaking, Augmented Reality and 3D as additional representational modes; reflect on how approach shapes meaning.
wider: Map the movements of a dance sequence visually — represent shapes, levels and energy as an abstract artwork; reflect on how colour, tone and composition communicate the mood and emotions of the dance
Explore Augmented Reality face filters — identify key asset types, design an analog concept for a filter communicating an intended idea, consider how it could extend a performance context

response_modes.reason: Students who have only used one representational approach (typically observational drawing) cannot reason about which approach is best suited to a given communicative purpose. The range of approaches — gestural, photographic, abstract, digital — reveals that mode is a choice, not a given.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Cross-arts visual mapping (dance-to-image) and AR filter design are genuinely novel representational contexts — they extend students' understanding of what visual arts can represent and how, in ways that feed directly into more sophisticated making.
success_criteria: Uses at least two different approaches to represent the same subject
Describes at least one thing each approach can communicate that the other cannot

nodes.label: Informed making choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can draw on documented experiments and reflection to make informed choices about visual conventions, processes and materials for a specific artwork.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one choice (convention, material or process) for an artwork that is directly informed by something discovered in a documented experiment.
nodes.typical_width: Use documented experiments to make and justify multiple informed choices for artworks; connect discoveries about representational approaches, material properties and visual effects to specific making decisions.
wider: Develop a range of 3D hand-building techniques in earthenware or modelling clay — document surface decoration experiments and reflect on how form and surface choices communicate ideas
Review a full set of documented experiments and identify a pattern in your choices — describe an emerging preference or approach that could define a personal style direction

response_modes.reason: The connection between documented discovery and future making is the core integration at this level — students demonstrate that experimentation is not separate from creating but feeds it.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one making choice that is directly informed by a documented experiment
Explains the connection between the discovery and the choice
